title: ～ふりをする — pretending to ～
summary: Means acting as if something were true when it is not. It follows the plain form of a verb, a noun + の, or an adjective (な-adjectives take な).

patterns.form: V普通形／Nの／Aい／Aな＋ふりをする
patterns.gloss: Plain form, N+の, い-adj, な-adj+な + ふりをする

body.p: ふり means an outward appearance or act. ふりをする is to put on that act on purpose. Negative forms and ～ている are very common: 知らないふり (pretending not to know), 寝ているふり (pretending to be asleep).
It always suggests intention. To say something merely looks a certain way, use ～ようだ or ～みたいだ instead. The pretender can be you or someone else.

examples.ja: 彼（かれ）は知（し）らないふりをした。
examples.romaji: Kare wa shiranai furi o shita.

examples.ja: 眠（ねむ）くなかったが、寝（ね）ているふりをした。
examples.romaji: Nemukunakatta ga, nete iru furi o shita.
examples.tr: I wasn't sleepy, but I pretended to be asleep.

examples.ja: 話（はなし）が聞（き）こえたのに、聞（き）こえないふりをした。
examples.romaji: Hanashi ga kikoeta noni, kikoenai furi o shita.
examples.tr: Even though I heard the conversation, I pretended not to hear it.

pitfalls: 知らないふり (acting) is not the same as 知らないようだ (it seems he doesn't know). The first is deliberate.
Add の after a noun: 病気のふり, not 病気ふり.
